identity.title: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis following CRISPR/Cas9 knockdown demonstrates a novel role for human T cell-intrinsic IL-1beta in determining T cell metabolic landscape.

content.abstract: T helper 17 (Th17) CD4+ T cells are key mediators of autoimmune pathology. Interleukin (IL)-1beta is a potent proinflammatory cytokine known to promote Th17 differentiation and pathogenicity, in combination with other cytokines. Whereas recent studies have shown that T cells are capable of expressing IL-1beta themselves, the role of this T cell-endogenous IL-1beta is poorly understood. Using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of IL1B in naive human CD4+ T cells along with cytokine neutralization and IL-1 receptor blockade, we found that T cell-intrinsic IL-1beta is not essential for Th17 differentiation or effector resistance. Remarkably, single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that IL1B deletion profoundly rewires the transcriptional and metabolic landscape within the T cells, suppressing glycolytic and hypoxia-responsive pathways. These findings uncouple T cell-intrinsic IL-1beta from Th17 effector resistance while uncovering an important contribution toward sustaining metabolic roles. This refines our understanding of IL-1beta biology and informs therapeutic strategies in immune-mediated disease settings.
